docs.title: Cobblemon: Hyperspace & Wormholes
docs.text:
Cobblemon: Hyperspace & Wormholes is a Cobblemon addon adding the Ultra Warp Ride from Pokémon USUM & my take on Hyperspace from Pokémon Legends ZA.

Hyperspaces can be visited using Distortion Splicers or by feeding your Hoopa donuts. You'll be taken to a version of your world containing different Pokémon. There are also tasks to complete while you are there.

Wormholes can be opened by Solgaleo, Lunala, the fused Necrozma and by a machine. You can find rare structures, Pokémon and Ultra Beasts through the Ultra Warp Ride.

You'll find a boss fight against Necrozma & Hoopa if you play in the different areas long enough.

docs.title: For Every Player
docs.text: Command What it does /stuck Only works inside Hyperspace. Ends your trip and sends you back to where you went in (or to the Overworld spawn if you have no trip). Your Pokémon are recalled first. /wormhole unstuck Only works during an Ultra Warp Ride. Ends the ride and takes you back on foot to where it started. Your mount goes back in its ball.

docs.title: For Server Operators
docs.text: You'll need operator permission (level 2) for these.

docs.title: /hyperspace
docs.text:
Command What it does /hyperspace createDistortion [options] Puts a spatial distortion on the wall in front of you (needs a 3x3 area). Only works in the Overworld. Anything you leave out is random. /hyperspace clearDistortions [radius] Removes distortions within the radius (default 128). /hyperspace locateDistortion Tells you where the nearest distortion within 500 blocks is. /hyperspace pity Shows your Hoopa pity (splices without Hoopa). /hyperspace pity set <amount> Sets your Hoopa pity. /hyperspace pity clear Clears your Hoopa pity. /hyperspace bossCleared <true\|false> [players] Marks players as having beaten Hoopa Unbound or not (pity and hard mode).

The createDistortion options can go in any order:

Option Example Notes type= / types= type=fire,water Up to 3 types. star= / stars= star=5 1 to 5. legendary= legendary=kyogre Puts that legendary behind it. Legendaries only. megaPokemon= megaPokemon=charizard Puts a Mega Evolved Pokémon behind it. boss=hoopa_unbound Makes it the Hoopa Unbound event. Can't be used with anything else.

You can only use one of type, legendary and megaPokemon at a time.

docs.title: /wormhole
docs.text:
Command What it does /wormhole create [destination] Opens a wormhole 12 blocks ahead that anyone can use, mounted or not. With no destination it starts an Ultra Warp Ride. /wormhole clearCooldown Clears your wormhole ride cooldown. /wormhole pity / pity set <amount> / pity clear Your Necrozma pity (white wormholes without Necrozma). /wormhole bossCleared <true\|false> [players] Marks players as having beaten Necrozma or not.

A destination is a world, with options in square brackets like vanilla block states:

  • Ultra Beast worlds - by id, for example ultra_jungle, ultra_deep_sea, ultra_desert, ultra_plant, ultra_crater, ultra_megalopolis.
  • The Ultra Space Wilds - by short name, cliff, crag, cave, water.
  • Options - rings= (0 to 3), pokemon= (a species), category= (Wilds only: regular, legendary, mythical, ultra_beast, paradox, or a Wilds world's name) and ride=true (starts a ride where every wormhole leads there, instead of taking you straight there). You can't use pokemon and category together.

Some examples are /wormhole create cliff[rings=3,category=legendary] and /wormhole create ultra_jungle[pokemon=buzzwole].

docs.title: /boss
docs.text: Command What it does /boss spawn <bossName> Spawns a boss 4 blocks in front of you, facing you. Bosses: hoopa_unbound, necrozma_megalopolis. /boss setHP <boss> <percentage> Sets a boss's shared HP. <boss> is an entity selector or UUID (tab-complete while looking at it). /boss despawn <boss> Removes a boss.

docs.title: FAQ & Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Where do I find Spatial Distortions?

They only show up in the Overworld, on walls like cliffs and hills, 64 to 160 blocks away from you. Walk around and look at cliffs. They're a lot easier to find with Xaero's Minimap & World Map or JourneyMap.

How do I get a Hoopa?

Beat the Hoopa Unbound event and catch the Hoopa it leaves. That's the only way in H&W.

How do I get Solgaleo or Lunala?

Get Cosmog from the Item Analyser, then evolve it. You can learn more here.

Does Legendary Monuments replace the legendary wormholes?

No. Legendary Monuments only takes its own legendaries out of Hyperspace. If you only want legendaries from Legendary Monuments, turn off Wormhole Legendaries in the Settings.

I'm stuck, what do I do?

Use /stuck in Hyperspace, or /wormhole unstuck in a wormhole.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
Cobblemon: Hyperspace & Wormholes has a few dependencies you'll need to install for this mod to work:

  • Fabric API
  • Fabric Language Kotlin
  • Cobblemon
  • Mega Showdown
  • AllTheMons x Mega Showdown

Once you have all of those mods installed, there are also some optional mods that H&W supports:

  • Mod Menu - opens the H&W settings screen.
  • Xaero's Minimap & World Map, or JourneyMap - spatial distortions show up on your map.
  • Waystones - give your legend a Warp Stone and it can fly you to your waystones.
  • CobbleDollars - Floating Poké Balls give you money when you pop them.
  • Legendary Monuments - purple wormholes can take you to its shrines.
  • Dungeons and Taverns - more places for purple wormholes to take you.
  • Reactive Music - turned down while Hyperspace music is playing.
  • CobbleNav - shows which Pokémon you can find on your Hyperspace trip.

docs.title: Accessing Hyperspace
docs.text:
You can access Hyperspace with Hoopa or Distortion Splicers.

With Distortion Splicers:

  1. Craft Distortion Splicers with the recipe.
  2. Locate a Hyperspace Distortion. Can find easier with Xaero's Minimap & Worldmap installed.
  3. Right-Click distortion with the splicers.
  4. Walk into distortion.

With Hoopa:

  1. Cook up a donut.
  2. Locate a Hyperspace Distortion.
  3. Send out your Hoopa, then feed it a donut.
  4. Walk into distortion.

Warning

Opened Distortions remain open for 15s. Players need to enter it during that time otherwise the item is wasted. Distortion Splicers set a random allocated time inside the Hyperspace between 90s and 5 minutes. If you don't leave quick enough, your armour will lose a lot of durability and you'll take a bit of damage too.

Distortions only show up in the Overworld, on cliffs and other walls 64 to 160 blocks away from you. You can learn more about finding them here.

docs.title: Inside Hyperspace
docs.text: Hyperspace has some quirks to it, such as your Pokémon's levels increasing above Level 100. The level changes are temporary and revert to normal upon exiting.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text: You'll notice some tasks on the top left of your screen. These tasks reward you with EXP Candy, as well as some other items if you finish them all and pop the Golden Poké Ball.

docs.title: Floating Poké Balls
docs.text:
There are Floating Poké Balls scattered across each Hyperspace. Popping them can reward you with many different items. You'll need to send out a Pokémon and use moves on them by pressing down middle click to pop them.

When you are finished with that Hyperspace, you simply need to return to the distortion and walk through it.

You can learn more about Quick Battles, Floating Poké Balls and other quirks of Hyperspace here.

docs.title: Accessing Ultra Space
docs.text:
Ultra Space is a bit more difficult to access, requiring a machine early on. You can learn about accessing Ultra Space in more detail here, otherwise here is a basic rundown:

  1. Build an Item Analyser by putting a Cobblemon Data Monitor on top of a Fossil Analyzer.
  2. Craft an Empty Jar and keep it in your inventory. Using the Item Analyser can fill it up with cosmic energy.
  3. Once the jar is full, put it in the Item Analyser with a Golden Apple and charge the machine with lightning or an Electric move. Out comes Cosmog!
  4. Raise Cosmog into Solgaleo or Lunala.
  5. Fly on your Solgaleo or Lunala and press V to open a wormhole, then fly into it to start the Ultra Warp Ride.

Coloured wormholes take you to the Ultra Space Wilds, white ones to the Ultra Beast worlds and purple ones to a rare structure in your world.

docs.title: Bosses
docs.text: If you keep splicing distortions you'll eventually run into Hoopa Unbound, and if you keep going through white wormholes you'll find Necrozma. Beat them and you get to catch your own.

docs.title: Cobblemon Blocks The Mod Uses
docs.text:
The Item Analyser machine is built on the Item Analyser, which is just Cobblemon's Fossil Analyzer renamed. The Data Monitor goes on top of it and gets charged by lightning or Electric moves. When a Data Monitor breaks it turns into a Damaged Data Monitor, and you can repair it with 8 Iron Ingots. You can learn more about the machine here.

Type gems go into the Item Analyser recipe (with Blaze Powder), and the Psychic and Dark Gems are also used for the Distortion Splicer.

docs.title: Items From Other Mods
docs.text: Beating Hoopa Unbound gives you a Prison Bottle (Mega Showdown), once per player. Beating a Mega Evolved Pokémon in a 4 star Hyperspace gives you its Mega Stone (Mega Showdown and other Mega mods).

docs.title: What You Need
docs.text:
H&W is for Minecraft 1.21.1 and has to be installed on both the client and the server. You'll need:

What Version Java 21 or newer Fabric Loader 0.16.0 or newer Fabric API Any Fabric Language Kotlin Any Cobblemon 1.8.4 Mega Showdown 1.3.3 AllTheMons x Mega Showdown Any

The Necrozma and Hoopa Unbound models come from your Mega Showdown files. They're tested with Mega Showdown 1.3.3, so with a different version some of them may be missing.

docs.title: Works With
docs.text:
You don't need any of these, but H&W supports them if you have them installed:

  • CobbleDollars - Floating Poké Balls give you money when you pop them.
  • Legendary Monuments - purple wormholes can take you to its shrines, and the legendaries it has shrines for are left out of Hyperspace. You can learn more about that here.
  • Waystones - give your legend a Warp Stone and it can fly you through a tunnel to your waystones. There are no waystones in Ultra Space.
  • Xaero's Minimap & World Map, or JourneyMap - spatial distortions show up on your map and minimap, with their stars and types when you hover them.
  • Reactive Music - turned down while Hyperspace music is playing.
  • Mod Menu - opens the H&W settings screen. You can learn more about the settings here.
  • Dungeons and Taverns - more places for purple wormholes to take you.
  • CobbleNav - shows which Pokémon you can find on your Hyperspace trip.

docs.title: CobbleDollars
docs.text:
With CobbleDollars installed, Floating Poké Balls give you money too. It's 2,500 per ball and 10,000 per golden ball, times stars/5, so a normal ball gives 500 to 2,500.

Modpacks can change this loot with a datapack. You can learn more about that here.

docs.title: Bosses
docs.text:
Beating Hoopa Unbound gets each player a Hoopa Confined (level 70) and the Hoopa: Unbound advancement. Anyone who never had a Prison Bottle gets one too.

Beating Necrozma gets each player in the party a Necrozma (level 70) and the Light Recaptured advancement.

docs.title: What Most People Change
docs.text:
• Shiny Odds - for more (or fewer) shiny Pokémon from wormholes, change the odds for 0, 1, 2 and 3 rings. Going from 100 to 50 on Shiny Odds: No Rings doubles the no-ring chance from 1% to 2%.
  • Legendaries - each way of getting legendaries has its own switch under Legendaries. With Wormhole Legendaries off, Wilds wormholes only lead to regular Pokémon.
  • Legendaries only from Legendary Monuments - turn Hyperspace Legendaries and Wormhole Legendaries off, and keep the Legendary Monuments setting on Monuments.
  • Data Monitor Griefing - turn it off if you don't want Data Monitors breaking.
  • Max Distortions Per Player - raise it to see more spatial distortions around. At 4 you keep up to 4 around you in busy areas.
  • Distortion Star Weight - raise a rank's weight to make it more common, for example 5 Star from 5 to 20.
  • Total Distortions for Hoopa Boss and Total White Wormholes for Necrozma Boss - lower them to find Hoopa Unbound or Necrozma sooner, for example from 12 to 6.

Which Pokémon come out of each wormhole colour isn't a setting, you change that with a datapack. You can learn more about that here.

docs.title: The Settings Screen
docs.text:
With Mod Menu installed, open the mod's config button in your mod list to get the Hyperspace & Wormholes Settings screen. Every setting has a tooltip that explains it and gives an example, so just hover its name. Reset to Defaults puts everything back.

The screen edits config/hyperspace_wormholes_gameplay.json. On a server, the server's own settings file is used. The server sends its settings to every player who joins, so changing them in your own game only changes your single-player worlds.

docs.title: Bosses
docs.text: Setting Default What it does Total Distortions for Hoopa Boss 12 How many splices in a row without Hoopa before the next one is guaranteed. 0 turns pity off. Total White Wormholes for Necrozma Boss 12 How many white wormholes in a row without Necrozma before the next one is guaranteed. 0 turns pity off. Enable Hard Mode? Off On: bosses are always in hard mode. Off: a boss is only in hard mode for players who have beaten it.

docs.title: Wormholes
docs.text:
Setting Default What it does Shiny Odds: No Rings 1 in 100 The shiny chance of a regular Pokémon past a wormhole with no rings, and of regular Item Analyser Pokémon. Shiny Odds: 1 Ring 1 in 10 The shiny chance with 1 ring, after flying 5,000 light-years or more. Shiny Odds: 2 Rings 1 in 5 The same with 2 rings (20%). Shiny Odds: 3 Rings 1 in 3 The same with 3 rings (33%). Legendary Shiny Odds 0 The shiny chance of legendary, mythical and paradox Pokémon past a wormhole or from the Item Analyser. 0 uses Cobblemon's own shiny rate. Ultra Beast Shiny Odds 0 The same for Ultra Beasts. Data Monitor Griefing On Whether lightning and Pokémon moves can break Data Monitors. It shows "Custom" if the file has the three switches set differently.

The shiny odds are written as "1 in N", so 100 is a 1% chance, 10 is 10%, 2 is 50%, 1 is always and 0 is never. The ring odds are what you get after a long ride. Below 5,000 light-years, a wormhole with rings has a chance between the no-ring odds and its own. It goes up every 500 light-years, like in Ultra Sun & Ultra Moon. You can find that table here. Legendaries and Ultra Beasts have their own two settings, which use Cobblemon's normal shiny rate unless you change them.

Updating from 2.0.2 or older

Older versions had Base Shiny Chance (a percent) and Multiplier Per Ring. The first time 2.1.0 starts, it works out the four odds from them and writes the new ones to the file. That way, odds you changed carry over. A file still on the old defaults gets the new defaults (2 and 3 rings were 1 in 5.26 and 1 in 2.78, now 1 in 5 and 1 in 3).

docs.title: Legendaries
docs.text:
Setting Default What it does Hyperspace Legendaries On Whether a legendary can appear on a Hyperspace trip (the 5% on 5-star distortions). Megas still come. Wormhole Legendaries On Whether a legendary can wait past a red, green, yellow or blue wormhole in the Ultra Space Wilds. Ultra Beasts aren't affected. Catch Beaten Bosses On Whether you can catch Hoopa and Necrozma after beating them. Off: the boss leaves once it's beaten, but Hoopa's Prison Bottle still drops. Cosmog Summon On Whether the Item Analyser summons Cosmog from a full Jar of Cosmic Energy and a Golden Apple. Off: you can't get Solgaleo and Lunala, the Ultra Warp Ride mounts, this way. Operator commands that ask for a set legendary (/hyperspace createDistortion legendary=..., /wormhole create) still work with these off.

If you only want legendaries from Legendary Monuments, turn Hyperspace Legendaries and Wormhole Legendaries off and keep Legendary Monuments on Monuments. Leave Catch Beaten Bosses on if you still want to catch Hoopa and Necrozma, and leave Cosmog Summon on, since that's how you get a mount for the Ultra Warp Ride.

docs.title: How Boss Fights Work
docs.text: H&W has two boss fights: Hoopa Unbound in Hyperspace and Necrozma on the Megalo Tower. They both work the same way.

docs.title: Starting A Fight
docs.text:
Up to 4 players can fight a boss together.

  1. Right-click the boss to get ready.
  2. Once every player there who can battle has right-clicked it, a screen transition plays.
  3. Everyone is moved to their spot in front of the boss and the fight starts.

If you're already in a battle you'll get "You're already in a battle.". If you have no healthy Pokémon, you'll get "You have no Pokémon able to battle."

docs.title: One Shared Battle
docs.text:
Each player has their own normal Cobblemon battle, but they all count as one fight.

The boss has one shared HP pool: its normal max HP times 10 per player (so 10x solo, 20x with two, 30x with three and 40x with four). The HP bar at the top shows its name, level, HP, stat changes and status.

Each round waits for everyone to pick a move ("Waiting for all moves to be selected…"). The boss attacks once per round, going for whichever player's Pokémon it can hurt the most. Moves that hit all foes, like Earthquake, hit every player's Pokémon. Everyone sees everyone's moves in their battle log.

The boss uses Cobblemon's strongest battle AI and starts with +1 in its highest stat. At some HP marks it changes form or calls in help (each boss's page has the details). A big hit can skip past a mark. If nobody fights it for 2 minutes it heals back to full.

docs.title: Banned Moves
docs.text:
Some moves are greyed out against bosses ("This move cannot be used in this battle."):

Fissure, Sheer Cold, Guillotine, Horn Drill, Endeavor, Pain Split, Final Gambit, Super Fang, Nature's Madness, Ruination, Guardian of Alola, Destiny Bond, Perish Song.

One-hit KO moves from other mods are blocked too. If one gets through anyway (for example through Sleep Talk or Metronome), it doesn't work on the boss.

docs.title: Winning And Catching
docs.text:
A boss can't faint. When it gets to 1 HP it's beaten, the battles end and each player gets their own copy to catch. Throw any Poké Ball at yours and it's caught. You can't see other players' copies.

Server owners can turn catching off with the Catch Beaten Bosses setting. The boss then just leaves once it's beaten, but Hoopa's Prison Bottle still drops.

docs.title: Hard Mode
docs.text:
If the player who starts the fight has beaten that boss before, it's in hard mode. Then it's level 100, it holds its type's boosting item (for example Twisted Spoon for a Psychic type), and its "+1 in its highest stat" goes to every stat instead.

Server owners can make hard mode always on with the Enable Hard Mode? setting.

docs.title: Pity
docs.text:
Each boss has a pity count. After 12 tries without meeting it, the next try always finds it. Pity stops once you've beaten that boss.

For Hoopa Unbound, every Distortion Splicer splice you open counts as a try. For Necrozma it's every white wormhole you enter.

Server owners can change the number or turn pity off. You can learn more about the boss settings here.

docs.title: Hoopa Unbound
docs.text: The Hoopa Unbound event is a boss fight inside Hyperspace. Beating it is the only way to get Hoopa, and it gives you a Prison Bottle too.

docs.title: Finding Hoopa Unbound
docs.text:
Hoopa Unbound shows up when you open distortions with a Distortion Splicer. Each splice has a 5% chance to be the event. Donut and Hoopa portals never lead to it. Neither do distortions an admin made with a set legendary or Mega.

After 12 splices in a row without it (counted for the player using the splicer), your next splice is always the event. This pity stops once you've beaten Hoopa Unbound.

Everyone who walks into that portal is part of the event. You can learn more about finding and opening distortions here.

docs.title: What Happens
docs.text:
1. You arrive on a special arena island (plains hills around a flat floor) instead of a copy of your world. At first it seems normal. The clock counts down and the tasks are up, but there are no wild Pokémon and the way home is small and can't be used.
  2. After about 10 seconds the clock and the task list turn into glitch text, the music tears apart and the HUD disappears.
  3. A giant ring opens in the sky and Hoopa Unbound comes down through it.
  4. Right-click Hoopa to get ready. The fight starts when everyone on the island who can battle has done that.

The trip timer stops during the event, and no wild Pokémon spawn on the island for as long as it lasts.

docs.title: The Fight
docs.text:
Hoopa Unbound is level 90 and knows Hyperspace Fury, Psychic, Dark Pulse, Focus Blast, Gunk Shot and Nasty Plot. It has 10x its normal HP per player and starts with +1 in its highest stat. If you're alone (nobody else entered that Hyperspace) you get 2 Pokémon out at once, otherwise 1.

You can learn more about the shared battle, banned moves and hard mode here.

At 80% HP the battles pause. Hoopa backs off and throws two rings. Volcanion and Zygarde (level 60) come out and take its place in every player's battle. At 40% HP it throws three: Dialga, Origin Forme Giratina and Palkia (level 80).

  • You still only have your usual number of Pokémon out, against all the called legendaries at once.
  • Each called legendary has one HP pool shared by all players (its normal HP times the number of players). Knock one out in one battle and it faints in all of them.
  • Beating them doesn't hurt Hoopa. Once they're all down, Hoopa comes back into the same battles with +1 in its second-lowest stat.
  • A hit big enough to go past both marks goes straight to the second wave, and a hit that beats Hoopa skips any waves that are left.

docs.title: Winning
docs.text:
Every battle ends and Hoopa turns back into Hoopa Confined (level 70) with the Prison Bottle effect. Each player gets their own Hoopa to catch. Throw any Poké Ball at it. You have about 3 minutes.

If you've never had a Prison Bottle (Mega Showdown's item), one is left lying on the floor for you. Only you can pick yours up, and you only ever get one.

Server owners can turn catching off with the Catch Beaten Bosses setting. Hoopa then just leaves, but the Prison Bottle still drops.

Everyone on the island is marked as having beaten Hoopa Unbound, so no more pity and hard mode next time. Then Hoopa leaves, the sky ring closes and the way home opens. There's no time limit. You also get the Hoopa: Unbound advancement.

docs.title: Losing Or Leaving
docs.text:
If nobody on the island can battle any more, the event ends the same way but without a Hoopa to catch.

Warning

Using a Distortion Splicer during the event ends it. Hoopa leaves and everyone is pulled towards the way home, harder every second. This still uses one of the splicer's uses.

After the event the task list and the music stay off until you leave Hyperspace.

docs.title: Necrozma
docs.text: The Necrozma boss fight happens at the top of the Megalo Tower in the Ultra Megalopolis. Beating it is the only way to get Necrozma. It never comes out of a wormhole or the Item Analyser.

docs.title: Finding Necrozma
docs.text:
Fly the Ultra Warp Ride far enough for white wormholes to show up (after 4,500 light-years). Each white wormhole has about a 1% chance to lead to the Ultra Megalopolis, no matter how many rings it has.

After 12 white wormholes in a row without it, your next white wormhole always goes there. This pity stops once you've beaten Necrozma.

docs.title: Starting The Fight
docs.text:
Dusk Mane Necrozma or Dawn Wings Necrozma (it's a coin flip each time) stands on the round stage at the top. It doesn't move and can't be hurt or caught yet. A Poké Ball thrown at it gets knocked away ("The light around Necrozma knocks the ball away!").

Right-click it to get ready. Every player nearby has to click it, and the first 4 make up the party. Players can't stand on the floor under the stage.

docs.title: The Fight
docs.text:
Dusk Mane Necrozma Dawn Wings Necrozma Level 72 72 Moves Sunsteel Strike, Photon Geyser, Earthquake, Dragon Dance, Stone Edge, Knock Off Moongeist Beam, Photon Geyser, Power Gem, Calm Mind, Earth Power, Heat Wave

It has 10x its normal HP per player and starts with +1 in its highest stat. You can learn more about the shared battle, banned moves and hard mode here.

At 50% HP the battles pause for the Ultra Burst scene, and it becomes Ultra Necrozma. Ultra Necrozma is level 100 and gets another +1 in its highest stat. It knows Photon Geyser, Dragon Pulse, Power Gem, Earthquake, Heat Wave and Knock Off. It also has its own version of Neuroforce for this fight. It powers up its super-effective attacks, and the light of the Megalo Tower raises its Attack, Defense, Sp. Atk, Sp. Def and Speed by half.

At 33% HP it uses its Z-Move, Light That Burns the Sky, once, and it hits every player's Pokémon. In hard mode it uses it a second time below 11% HP.

docs.title: Winning
docs.text:
At 1 HP every battle ends as a win, and Necrozma powers down to its normal form. Each player in the party who's still at the top gets their own weakened Necrozma to catch. It's level 70 with Prism Armor and knows Photon Geyser, Power Gem, Iron Defense and Night Slash. Throw any Poké Ball at yours.

Warning

If you're away from the top for 30 seconds you lose your copy.

Server owners can turn catching off with the Catch Beaten Bosses setting, and then Necrozma just leaves once it's beaten.

Everyone in the fight is marked as having beaten Necrozma, so no more pity and hard mode next time. You also get the Light Recaptured advancement.

docs.title: Losing
docs.text:
If every battle is lost, a new fused Necrozma comes back on the stage. You can click it again after 10 seconds.

The fight also ends if everyone leaves the Ultra Megalopolis. Like every Ultra Space world, it resets when the world loads.

docs.title: Datapacks
docs.text: A lot of H&W can be changed with a datapack, so modpacks and servers can make it their own.

docs.title: What You Can Change
docs.text:
What File Page Hyperspace spawns data/hyperspace_wormholes/tags/pokemon/hyperspace.json Pokémon Tags Hyperspace legendaries data/hyperspace_wormholes/tags/pokemon/legendaries.json Pokémon Tags Who takes donuts data/hyperspace_wormholes/tags/pokemon/can_feed_donut.json Pokémon Tags Item Analyser Pokémon The same wormhole_pools files as the wormholes Wormhole Pokémon Pools Ultra Space Wilds Pokémon (red, green, yellow and blue wormholes) data/hyperspace_wormholes/wormhole_pools/<colour>.json Wormhole Pokémon Pools Floating Poké Ball loot data/hyperspace_wormholes/loot_table/gameplay/floating_poke_ball.json and golden_floating_poke_ball.json Floating Poké Ball Loot Boss fights data/<namespace>/bosses/<id>.json Boss Fights

The mod's own files are inside the mod's jar under data/hyperspace_wormholes/. You can open the jar like a zip and copy one to start from.

docs.title: Making A Datapack
docs.text:
A datapack is a folder (or a zip of that folder) with a pack.mcmeta file and a data folder in it:

my-hw-pack/
├── pack.mcmeta
└── data/
    └── hyperspace_wormholes/
        ├── tags/pokemon/hyperspace.json
        ├── wormhole_pools/red.json
        ├── loot_table/gameplay/floating_poke_ball.json
        └── bosses/hoopa_unbound.json

You only need the files you want to change. Folder and file names have to be lowercase.

pack.mcmeta tells Minecraft it's a datapack. For Minecraft 1.21.1 the pack_format is 48:

{
  "pack": {
    "pack_format": 48,
    "description": "My H&W changes"
  }
}

docs.title: Installing It
docs.text:
1. Put the folder or zip in your world's datapacks folder. In singleplayer, click Edit on your world then Open World Folder. On a server it's world/datapacks.
  2. Run /reload, or restart the world.

You can check it loaded with /datapack list. If a file has a mistake in it, the game log says which file.

Note

Datapacks only go on the server (or in your singleplayer world). Players joining a server don't need them.

docs.title: Boss Fights
docs.text:
Every boss is set by a boss file. You can change Hoopa Unbound and Necrozma with a datapack, or make your own boss.

Boss File Hoopa Unbound data/hyperspace_wormholes/bosses/hoopa_unbound.json Necrozma data/hyperspace_wormholes/bosses/necrozma_megalopolis.json Your own data/<namespace>/bosses/<id>.json

Your file replaces the mod's whole file, so copy the mod's one and change what you want. Every key can be left out. Anything you leave out uses its default.

You can learn more about how boss fights work here.

docs.title: Your Own Boss
docs.text:
A new boss file doesn't show up in the world by itself. An operator spawns it with /boss spawn <id>, for example /boss spawn mypack:mewtwo. Bosses in the hyperspace_wormholes namespace only need the id, like /boss spawn hoopa_unbound.

It stays where it was spawned. Players join the fight by starting a battle with it like a wild Pokémon. Once it's beaten, everyone still in the fight can throw a Poké Ball in their own battle to catch their own copy of it.

docs.title: Main Keys
docs.text:
Key What it does Default name The name on the boss's HP bar. Plain text or a translation key. The species name spawn_species The species /boss spawn makes it from. It goes in front of properties. None properties The boss Pokémon, written like Cobblemon's /pokespawn (species, level, form and so on). None moves Up to 6 moves it uses in the fight, instead of its own. Its own moves hp_per_trainer Its HP is its normal max HP times this, times the number of players. 5 scaling A list of HP multipliers for 1, 2, 3 and 4 players, used instead of hp_per_trainer. With more players than entries, the last one is used. None max_trainers How many players can fight it at once. 4 scale Its size. 1 is normal size. 1.5 with /boss spawn, 1 for Hoopa and Necrozma ai_skill How smart it battles, up to 5 (smartest). 5 boosts Stat stages it gets at the start of the fight. See Boosts. None music Its battle music, as a sound event id. Cobblemon's normal battle music ultimate A big move it uses once at low HP. See Ultimate. None forms Form changes at HP marks. See Forms. None variants Named versions of the boss, each with its own name, properties, moves and music. See Variants. None defeated_properties Cobblemon properties put on it once it's beaten, so the one you catch can be different. None banned_moves Moves players' Pokémon can't use against it. Your list replaces the default one, and [] bans nothing. The 13 moves here opening_transition_seconds Hoopa and Necrozma only. How long the screen transition before the fight lasts. The music starts with it. 0

Moves, abilities and items are written in lowercase with no spaces, like darkpulse or megaloneuroforce.

The defaults for hp_per_trainer, max_trainers, scale and ai_skill come from config/hyperspace_wormholes_boss.json, so a server can change them for every boss that doesn't set its own.

docs.title: Boosts
docs.text:
boosts is a list of stats and how many stages each one goes up (or down, with a minus number):

"boosts": {"highest": 1, "spe": 1}

The stats are atk, def, spa, spd, spe, accuracy and evasion. highest is whichever of its stats is highest. In hard mode, highest goes to every stat instead.

docs.title: Ultimate
docs.text:
The ultimate is a move it uses once when its HP drops below a mark. It hits every player's Pokémon at once.

"ultimate": {"move": "photongeyser", "zmove": true, "hp_below": 0.33, "hard_again_below": 0.11}
Key What it does Default move The move. You need this one. None zmove true uses it as that move's Z-Move. It needs a Z-Crystal for that, see z_item below. false hp_below It's used when its HP drops below this much of its max. 0.33 is 33%. 0.33 hard_again_below In hard mode, it's used a second time below this mark. 0 turns that off. 0

docs.title: Forms
docs.text:
forms is a list of form changes. Each one happens once its HP drops below its hp_below mark. Its HP stays at the same percent when it changes. A form only needs the keys it changes.

Key What it does Default hp_below It changes when its HP drops below this much of its max. 0.5 is 50%. 0.5 name A new name for the HP bar. Keeps the old one properties Cobblemon properties put on it, which changes how it looks. None species The species it battles as, written the way Pokémon Showdown does, like Necrozma-Ultra. No change level A new level. No change ability A new ability. No change item The item it battles with. No change held_item An item id it really holds, like mega_showdown:ultranecrozium_z. No change z_item A Z-Crystal it counts as holding for Z-Moves only, so its real held item stays. None moves New moves, up to 6. No change boosts Stat stages it gets when it changes. None music New battle music. No change ultimate Its own ultimate, used instead of the main one. The main one

Note

In Hoopa's fight, the first two forms are only used for the HP marks where it calls in legendaries (80% and 40% by default). Their other keys don't do anything there, and which legendaries come out can't be changed.

docs.title: Variants
docs.text:
variants is how Necrozma comes as Dusk Mane or Dawn Wings. Its fight flips a coin between the dusk and dawn variants, so keep those two names in Necrozma's file. /boss spawn picks a variant at random too, but only uses its properties.

"variants": {
  "dusk": {
    "name": "Dusk Mane Necrozma",
    "properties": "prism_fusion=dusk moves=sunsteelstrike,photongeyser,earthquake,dragondance",
    "moves": ["sunsteelstrike", "photongeyser", "earthquake", "dragondance", "stoneedge", "knockoff"]
  },
  "dawn": {
    "name": "Dawn Wings Necrozma",
    "properties": "prism_fusion=dawn moves=moongeistbeam,photongeyser,powergem,calmmind",
    "moves": ["moongeistbeam", "photongeyser", "powergem", "calmmind", "earthpower", "heatwave"]
  }
}

docs.title: Necrozma Only
docs.text:
These only do something in the Necrozma fight. Ticks are 1/20 of a second.

Key What it does Default power_up_ticks How long the Ultra Burst scene lasts. 80 defeat_ticks How long the defeat scene lasts. 240 defeat_form_ticks When in the defeat scene defeated_properties go on. Same as defeat_ticks defeat_effect A Mega Showdown effect played in the defeat scene: id (the effect), at (the tick it starts on) and aspects (what it changes). None

Warning

The scene timings are made to match Necrozma's animations and music. If you change them, the scenes can cut off early or hang.

docs.title: Server Config Overrides
docs.text:
Server owners can also change single keys without a datapack. Put a file in config/hyperspace_wormholes/bosses/ named after the boss, like hoopa_unbound.json (or mypack__mewtwo.json for another namespace). Only the keys in it change, and they win over datapacks.

{"max_trainers": 2}

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
This is a Mewtwo boss that gets faster and stronger at half HP.

data/mypack/bosses/mewtwo.json:

{
  "name": "Mewtwo",
  "properties": "mewtwo level=80",
  "moves": ["psystrike", "aurasphere", "icebeam", "flamethrower", "calmmind", "recover"],
  "scaling": [8, 16, 24, 32],
  "scale": 1.5,
  "boosts": {"highest": 1},
  "ultimate": {"move": "psystrike", "hp_below": 0.25},
  "forms": [
    {
      "hp_below": 0.5,
      "name": "Enraged Mewtwo",
      "moves": ["psystrike", "aurasphere", "thunderbolt", "shadowball", "nastyplot", "recover"],
      "boosts": {"spe": 1, "spa": 1}
    }
  ],
  "defeated_properties": "level=70"
}

Run /reload, then spawn it with /boss spawn mypack:mewtwo.

docs.title: Floating Poké Ball Loot
docs.text:
You can change what Floating Poké Balls drop with a datapack. They use normal Minecraft loot tables:

Ball File Floating Poké Ball data/hyperspace_wormholes/loot_table/gameplay/floating_poke_ball.json Golden Floating Poké Ball data/hyperspace_wormholes/loot_table/gameplay/golden_floating_poke_ball.json

Your file replaces the mod's file, so put in everything you want the ball to drop. You can see what the mod's tables drop here.

If you haven't made a loot table before, you can learn more about them on the Minecraft Wiki. Keep "type": "minecraft:chest" at the top.

docs.title: How It's Used
docs.text:
• Popping a ball rolls its loot table once. The mod's tables have 1 to 3 rolls, but that's up to your file.
  • Item Power can switch a normal ball to the golden table.
  • Big Haul rolls the table again for each extra item, and keeps the first item from each of those rolls.
  • The CobbleDollars money isn't part of the loot table, so a datapack can't change it.

You can learn more about Item Power and Big Haul here.

docs.title: Star Condition And Function
docs.text:
H&W adds a condition and a function so loot can go by the trip's stars. You can use them anywhere in the table.

hyperspace_wormholes:hoopa_stars is a condition. It only lets an entry (or pool) through when the trip's stars are between min and max:

Option What it does Default min The lowest stars it works on. 1 max The highest stars it works on. 5 
{"condition": "hyperspace_wormholes:hoopa_stars", "min": 3, "max": 4}

hyperspace_wormholes:hoopa_stars_count is a function. It shrinks item counts on lower star trips: x0.2 at 1 star, x0.4 at 2, up to the full amount at 5 stars. It never goes below 1. It has no options:

{"function": "hyperspace_wormholes:hoopa_stars_count"}

Note

These go by the stars of the player who popped the ball. Outside a Hyperspace trip, they count as 5 stars.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
This makes normal balls drop Rare Candy or diamonds, with a small chance of a Master Ball on 5 star trips. The diamond count goes down on lower star trips (4-12 at 5 stars, 1-3 at 1 star).

data/hyperspace_wormholes/loot_table/gameplay/floating_poke_ball.json:

{
  "type": "minecraft:chest",
  "functions": [{"function": "hyperspace_wormholes:hoopa_stars_count"}],
  "pools": [
    {
      "rolls": {"type": "minecraft:uniform", "min": 1, "max": 3},
      "entries": [
        {"type": "minecraft:item", "name": "cobblemon:rare_candy", "weight": 10},
        {
          "type": "minecraft:item",
          "name": "minecraft:diamond",
          "weight": 5,
          "functions": [{"function": "minecraft:set_count", "count": {"type": "minecraft:uniform", "min": 4, "max": 12}}]
        },
        {
          "type": "minecraft:item",
          "name": "cobblemon:master_ball",
          "weight": 1,
          "conditions": [{"condition": "hyperspace_wormholes:hoopa_stars", "min": 5}]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Pokémon Tags
docs.text:
H&W keeps a few lists of Pokémon, called Pokémon tags. You can change any of them with a datapack. They're all in data/hyperspace_wormholes/tags/pokemon/:

File What it's for hyperspace.json Wild Pokémon in Hyperspace legendaries.json Legendaries in Hyperspace can_feed_donut.json Pokémon you can feed a donut to

docs.title: The File
docs.text:
Every tag file looks the same:

{
  "replace": false,
  "values": [
    "snorlax",
    "munchlax"
  ]
}
Key What it does values The list of Pokémon. replace false adds your Pokémon to the mod's list. true throws the mod's list away and only uses yours. Leave it out for false.

Pokémon are written as Cobblemon's names for them, all lowercase with no spaces or dashes, like tapukoko, mrmime or farfetchd. You can also write the full id, like cobblemon:snorlax. Pokémon your Cobblemon doesn't have are just skipped.

If more than one datapack changes the same tag, they all add up. A pack with "replace": true throws away everything from the mod and the packs loaded before it.

Warning

These aren't quite normal Minecraft tags. You can't put other tags (#...) in the list, and every entry has to be a plain name, not {"id": ..., "required": false}. Forms (like vulpix alolan) don't work here, so use just the species name.

docs.title: Hyperspace Spawns
docs.text:
hyperspace.json is every wild Pokémon that can spawn in Hyperspace (866 species by default). Each trip picks 8 of them by the distortion's types and stars. You can learn more about how they're picked here.

Only Pokémon that can walk are used, and baby Pokémon never spawn. 1 star trips use first stages, 2 star trips use middle stages and Pokémon that don't evolve, and 3 to 5 star trips use fully evolved ones. So add whole evolution lines if you want them at every star.

This adds the Frigibax line to Hyperspace:

{
  "replace": false,
  "values": [
    "frigibax",
    "arctibax",
    "baxcalibur"
  ]
}

docs.title: Hyperspace Legendaries
docs.text:
legendaries.json is the legendaries that can wait on a 5 star Hyperspace trip. If one of them has the distortion's type, it gets picked. You can learn more about them here.

Only legendaries that can walk or fly are used. Cosmog, Cosmoem, Solgaleo and Lunala are never used. With Legendary Monuments installed and its setting on Monuments, the legendaries that have a shrine are left out too.

Anything in this tag also counts as a legendary for /hyperspace createDistortion legendary=....

This adds Mewtwo and Rayquaza:

{
  "replace": false,
  "values": [
    "mewtwo",
    "rayquaza"
  ]
}

Note

With the older wormhole colours (gameWormholeColours set to false in config/hyperspace_wormholes.json), gold wormholes use this tag too.

docs.title: Who Takes Donuts
docs.text:
can_feed_donut.json is the Pokémon you can feed a donut to at a spatial distortion to open it, like Hoopa. By default it's only Hoopa. You can learn more about feeding donuts here.

Use species names only, all lowercase.

This lets Snorlax and Munchlax open distortions too:

{
  "replace": false,
  "values": [
    "snorlax",
    "munchlax"
  ]
}

docs.title: Wormhole Pokémon Pools
docs.text:
You can change which Pokémon show up behind the red, green, yellow and blue wormholes with a datapack. Each colour has its own file:

Wormhole File Red data/hyperspace_wormholes/wormhole_pools/red.json Green data/hyperspace_wormholes/wormhole_pools/green.json Yellow data/hyperspace_wormholes/wormhole_pools/yellow.json Blue data/hyperspace_wormholes/wormhole_pools/blue.json

White wormholes (Ultra Beasts) can't be changed.

docs.title: The File
docs.text:
A file is just two lists of Pokémon names:

{
  "pokemon": [
    "swellow",
    "altaria",
    "yanmega"
  ],
  "legendaries": [
    "articuno",
    "zapdos",
    "moltres"
  ]
}

pokemon is the normal Pokémon, and legendaries is used when the wormhole gives you a legendary.

Your file replaces the mod's file for that colour, so put in every Pokémon you want, not just new ones. The mod's own files are inside the mod's jar under data/hyperspace_wormholes/wormhole_pools/, you can open the jar like a zip and copy one to start from.

docs.title: The Item Analyser
docs.text: The Item Analyser uses these files too. It picks from the pokemon lists of all four colours together, so changing a colour's file changes what the machine can give as well. It picks one with the gem's type if there is one, otherwise any of them.

docs.title: Extra Options
docs.text:
If you want more control over a Pokémon, write it like this instead of just the name:

{"pokemon": "dragonite", "weight": 3, "level": "60-70"}
Option What it does Example weight How often it shows up compared to the others. Normal is 1. 3 shows up 3 times as often as 1 level Its level, or a range. Leave it out for the normal level. "65" or "55-65" party It only shows up if you have these Pokémon in your party. ["kyogre", "groudon"]

You can mix both ways in the same list. Forms work too, like "ninetales alolan".

Note

Ultra Beasts, Cosmog, Cosmoem, Solgaleo, Lunala and Necrozma can't be added. Legendaries you already have show up less often.

docs.title: Example Datapack
docs.text:
This one makes red wormholes lead to Dragon types.

hw-dragon-wormholes.zip

hw-dragon-wormholes/
├── pack.mcmeta
└── data/hyperspace_wormholes/wormhole_pools/red.json

red.json:

{
  "pokemon": [
    "altaria",
    "flygon",
    "noivern",
    {"pokemon": "salamence", "level": "55-65"},
    {"pokemon": "dragonite", "weight": 0.5, "level": "60-70"}
  ],
  "legendaries": [
    "latias",
    "latios",
    {"pokemon": "rayquaza", "party": ["kyogre", "groudon"]}
  ]
}

To install it:

  1. Put the zip in your world's datapacks folder. In singleplayer, click Edit on your world then Open World Folder. On a server it's world/datapacks.
  2. Run /reload.

docs.title: Spatial Distortions
docs.text: Spatial distortions are how you get into Hyperspace, like in Legends: Z-A. They look like glowing holes on a wall.

docs.title: Where They Appear
docs.text:
Distortions only show up in the Overworld, never in the Nether, the End or modded dimensions. They need a wall: a solid face at least 3x3 blocks (a cliff, hillside or building, leaves don't count) with a clear 3x3 space in front of it, on solid dry ground.

They show up 64 to 160 blocks from a player, never within 32 blocks of one. Two distortions are always at least 48 blocks apart.

By default each player has up to 2 within 192 blocks in some areas of the map and 1 in others. Server owners can change it with Max Distortions Per Player in the settings.

A distortion lasts 60 minutes of game time before it fades, and new ones keep showing up as you move around. You can only open each one once. They're saved with the world, so they'll still be there after a restart.

docs.title: Stars And Types
docs.text:
Look at a distortion from within 7 blocks and you'll see its label: "Spatial Distortion", its stars (1 to 5) and its types (1 to 3).

The stars set the trip's wild Pokémon levels, the loot and how fast your donut's time burns. Here's the default chance of each (server owners can change it):

Stars Chance 1 35% 2 28% 3 20% 4 12% 5 5%

The types decide which Pokémon spawn on the island. A distortion has 1 type 40% of the time, 2 types 40% of the time and 3 types 20% of the time. They come from the biome it showed up in. If the biome has fewer, the rest are random:

Biome Types Deep Dark Ghost, Dark Swamps, bogs, marshes Poison, Water Oceans Water Rivers Water, Normal Beaches Water, Ground Mushroom Fields Psychic, Fairy Cherry, flower, meadow, lavender biomes Fairy, Grass Dark Forest, dead and spooky biomes Ghost, Dark Jungles Bug, Grass Deserts, dunes Ground, Fire Badlands Ground, Rock Ice, frozen, snowy, tundra biomes Ice Peaks, slopes, windswept, stony, crags Rock, Flying Savannas Normal, Fire Cave biomes Rock, Steel Forests, taigas Grass, Bug Anything else Normal, Grass

docs.title: Opening A Distortion
docs.text: You'll need to be within 8 blocks of the distortion (and within 6 blocks up or down). If you're not, you'll get "There isn't a Spatial Distortion nearby...". The mod won't tell you where the nearest one is unless you have a map mod installed.

docs.title: With Hoopa
docs.text:
You can only get Hoopa by beating the Hoopa Unbound event.

  1. Cook up a donut.
  2. Send out your Hoopa and right-click it with the donut. You can also right-click with the donut in your hand while Hoopa is in your party or out within 32 blocks.
  3. Hoopa comes out, eats the donut, charges up and throws its ring at the distortion, which opens into a portal.
  4. Walk into the portal.

If Hoopa is fainted or in a battle, the portal opens straight away without the scene. Without a Hoopa you'll get "You need a Hoopa with you to feed it a donut here".

The donut decides how long the trip lasts and gives it Flavor Powers. You can learn more about donuts here.

docs.title: With Distortion Splicers
docs.text:
1. Craft Distortion Splicers with the recipe below.
  2. Use the splicers near the distortion. They "splice" it open. That gives you the same kind of portal, but it flickers and isn't stable.
  3. Walk into the portal.

The Psychic Gem and Dark Gem are Cobblemon's type gems.

You don't need a Hoopa or a donut. Each splice uses one of the splicers' 4 uses. A splice trip has no Flavor Powers. Its time limit is hidden (the action bar shows "Time Remaining: ???") and is a random 90 to 300 seconds.

Warning

If time runs out while you're inside, you get pulled out. You lose half your max health (never below 1 HP) and 35% of each worn armour piece's durability, which can break it. Creative and spectator players aren't hurt. Leaving through the way home is safe.

Each splice has a 5% chance to be the Hoopa Unbound event instead of a normal trip.

docs.title: The Portal
docs.text:
The portal opens on the wall where the distortion was and stays open for 15 seconds, with a "Closes in" timer above it. Whoever opened it goes in first. Everyone who walks in during those 15 seconds goes to the same island and shares the same timer.

Sometimes a distortion won't open:

  • "The distortion needs solid ground to open on!" - there's no solid block under the portal spot.
  • "Something is in the way of the distortion!" - blocks are in the way of the portal.
  • "Hyperspace is full right now, try again soon!" - all 64 Hyperspace islands on the server are in use.

If Hoopa gets refused, you keep the donut.

docs.title: Maps
docs.text: If you have Xaero's Minimap, Xaero's World Map or JourneyMap installed, distortions show up as small icons on your map in the Overworld. Hover over one on the full map to see its stars and types. The icons are just for finding them. You can't fast travel with them.

docs.title: Donuts
docs.text:
Donuts are what you feed Hoopa at a spatial distortion to open it, like in Legends: Z-A. The donut sets how long the trip lasts and gives it Flavor Powers. Everyone who goes through that portal gets the same powers.

You can only get Hoopa by beating the Hoopa Unbound event.

docs.title: Cooking
docs.text:
Donuts are cooked in Cobblemon's Campfire Pot, in two steps:

  1. Make a Plain Donut from Wheat, Wheat, Egg and Sugar (in any order).
  2. Put the Plain Donut back in the pot with 1 to 8 berries around it to get a berry donut.

Any berries work, so there isn't only one way to make them. These are a few of them:

Each recipe makes one donut. A donut that already has berries can't go back in the pot, and the seasoning slots aren't used for donuts.

You can use any of Cobblemon's Cheri, Chesto, Pecha, Rawst, Aspear, Oran, Persim, Lum, Sitrus, Pomeg, Kelpsy, Qualot, Hondew, Grepa and Tamato berries, the 18 type-resist berries (Occa to Roseli), and the 18 Hyper Berries from Hyperspace.

Hold Shift over a berry to see what it adds to a donut. The "Donut Info" shows its calories, flavor score and which powers it gives.

docs.title: Names And Stars
docs.text:
A donut is named after the berry it has the most of and its strongest flavour, followed by its stars, like "Roseli Berry Meringue Donut ★★". Each flavour gives a different name:

  • Sweet - Meringue
  • Spicy - Curry
  • Sour - Jam
  • Bitter - Chocolate
  • Dry - Cream

If flavours tie for strongest, you get a Rainbow donut.

The stars come from the donut's flavour score, which is all its berries' flavour points added up:

Flavour score Stars 120 ★ 240 ★★ 350 ★★★ 700 ★★★★ 960 ★★★★★

You'll need Hyper Berries for 3 stars and up. The best normal berries have 40 flavour points, so 8 of them only get you to 320 (2 stars). Hyper Berries have 4 times the flavour of their normal berry and a lot more calories. They drop from Floating Poké Balls in Hyperspace.

docs.title: Calories And Trip Time
docs.text:
Your donut's tooltip shows its Calories. That's its berries' calories added up, then raised by 10% per donut star. So a 5 star donut has 1.5 times its berries' calories.

At a distortion, the calories buy you time at that distortion's rate. 1 calorie is 1 second at a 1 star distortion:

If your donut has one star fewer than the distortion, it burns 1.5 times as fast. Two or more stars fewer and it burns 2.5 times as fast. A trip always lasts at least 1 minute 30 seconds.

docs.title: Flavor Powers
docs.text:
Powers only come from the donut's strongest flavour. If two flavours tie for strongest, both give their powers. The number of points in that flavour sets the power level. Hold Shift over a donut to see its powers.

Strongest flavour Lv. 1 Lv. 2 Lv. 3 Powers Sweet 120 200 300 Alpha Power, plus Humungo (5+ berries) or Teensy (4 or fewer berries) Sweet 420 525 700 Sparkling Power replaces Alpha Power Sour 120 200 300 Item Power and Big Haul Dry 120 200 300 Encounter Power and Catching Power Spicy, Bitter - - - No powers (they still count towards stars)

Here's what each power does in Hyperspace at its default strength:

Power Lv. 1 Lv. 2 Lv. 3 Sparkling Power (shiny odds) +1 shiny roll +2 shiny rolls +3 shiny rolls Alpha Power (alpha odds; base 5%) 10% alpha 20% alpha 50% alpha Humungo Power (bigger Pokémon) size 1.0x to 1.5x 1.13x to 1.5x 1.38x to 1.5x Teensy Power (smaller Pokémon) size 0.5x to 1.0x 0.5x to 0.87x 0.5x to 0.62x Item Power (Floating Poké Ball rolls golden-ball loot) 25% 50% 100% Big Haul (extra items per Floating Poké Ball) +2 +3 +5 Encounter Power (more Pokémon around you; normally 9) +3 +6 +9 Catching Power (a failed Poké Ball throw catches anyway) 10% 20% 30%

Without Sparkling Power a trip has 1 shiny roll. Each roll is one chance at Cobblemon's shiny rate, so 4 rolls is about 4 times the normal shiny chance. Server owners can make each power stronger or weaker, or turn it off, in the Settings.

A Distortion Splicer trip has no donut, so it doesn't get any powers.

docs.title: Quick Battles
docs.text:
Quick battles let your sent-out Pokémon use its moves outside of a normal battle, like in Legends: Z-A. They work anywhere, not only in Hyperspace. You'll need them to:

  • Pop Floating Poké Balls in Hyperspace, since they can't be punched.
  • Finish the "Quick battle and defeat 5 Pokémon." task.
  • Charge (or break) a Data Monitor for the Item Analyser.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
1. Send out a Pokémon. It has to be within 48 blocks of you and not in a battle. If you've got several out, it uses the one in your selected party slot, or else the nearest one.
  2. Hold middle mouse while looking at a target. Your Pokémon's four moves show up as tiles at the bottom right.
  3. Press a move key (1, 2, 3 or 4 by default) to use that move.

Your Pokémon runs over to the target and uses the move.

You can rebind all of these to anything you like in Options > Controls > Key Binds, under the "Cobblemon: Hyperspace & Wormholes" section:

  • Target Pokeball/Pokemon - the key you hold to target something (middle mouse by default).
  • Quick Battle Move 1 to Quick Battle Move 4 - uses that move (1 to 4 by default).

You can target a wild Pokémon or a Floating Poké Ball up to about 8 blocks away. It has to be near your crosshair with nothing in the way. You can also target a Data Monitor block you're looking at. If the target key is also your pick-block key, pressing it on a normal block still picks the block.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Each use costs 1 PP. Then every move has a cooldown of 1 second plus 1 second per 10 power. So an 80-power move waits 9 seconds. The tile shows the seconds left in red.

Status moves can't be used, and neither can Counter, Mirror Coat, Metal Burst, Comeuppance, Shell Trap or Bide. You also can't target shiny wild Pokémon, or legendary, mythical, Ultra Beast or paradox Pokémon.

Damage works like normal Pokémon damage (level, power, attack against defence, same-type bonus, multi-hit moves). If the two Pokémon are more than 20 levels apart, the lower-level one faints straight away.

Your Pokémon takes 20% of its max HP as recoil. It doesn't if it knocked the target out, or if the move was super effective and the levels are within 5 of each other.

docs.title: The Island
docs.text:
Every trip gets its own Hyperspace island. It's a copy of the land around the distortion you went in at, floating in Hyperspace with a grey edge. You'll arrive in front of the way home, a portal set into a wall of the island.

You can't break or place blocks in Hyperspace, not even in creative mode, and buckets don't work either. A server can have up to 64 islands in use at once.

docs.title: Time Limit
docs.text:
The action bar shows your Time Remaining. When it hits zero you're sent back to where you went in. Splice trips show "Time Remaining: ???" instead.

To leave early, you simply need to walk into the way home. You can't walk straight back into it until you've stepped out of it once. Dying ends the trip too, and so does /stuck. You can learn more about commands here.

Your sent-out Pokémon are put back in their balls before every teleport.

docs.title: Levels
docs.text:
Wild Pokémon levels and the level of the Pokémon you catch both depend on the distortion's stars:

Stars Wild Pokémon level Level of Pokémon you catch ★ 101-120 13-19 ★★ 121-135 15-25 ★★★ 136-150 20-35 ★★★★ 151-165 35-43 ★★★★★ 166-185 50-56

While you're in Hyperspace, any party Pokémon below the trip's range is raised to a random level in that range. It goes back to its real level and EXP when you leave. Your Pokémon don't gain EXP in Hyperspace, and you can't use EXP Candy there.

A Pokémon you catch is set to the "caught" level in the table (legendaries are at least level 80). The mod raises Cobblemon's max level to 200, but outside Hyperspace Pokémon still stop gaining EXP at level 100.

docs.title: Which Pokémon Spawn
docs.text:
Cobblemon's normal spawning is turned off in Hyperspace. Each trip gets its own small pool instead. It's taken from the hyperspace Pokémon tag (866 species by default) and picked by the distortion's types and stars. At 1 star you only get first-stage Pokémon. At 2 stars it's middle stages and Pokémon that don't evolve, and from 3 stars up it's fully evolved ones. Baby Pokémon never spawn.

The pool has 8 species, sorted by base stat total:

Rarity Species in the pool Base stat total Chance per spawn Common 3 up to 340 60% Uncommon 2 341-460 28% Rare 2 461-540 10% Ultra-rare 1 541+ 2%

Up to 9 wild Pokémon stay around you (within 32 blocks), and new ones fill the gaps. Encounter Power raises that number.

A rare or ultra-rare spawn is a herd 10% of the time. That's a big alpha leader at the top of the level range, holding its type's gem. It comes with 3 to 5 of its pre-evolutions.

The alpha chance is 5%, more with Alpha Power. The shiny chance is your trip's shiny rolls at Cobblemon's shiny rate. You can learn more about Alpha Power and Sparkling Power here.

docs.title: Legendary And Mega Bosses
docs.text:
A 5 star distortion has a 5% chance to hold a legendary. Everyone who went through the portal gets their own copy at the middle of the island. A 4 star trip has a 10% chance of a Mega Evolved Pokémon spawning near you, rolled for each player as they enter.

When one is waiting you'll hear its cry with an echo, and you'll get an advancement as you enter ("A Legendary Encounter" or "Untapped Power").

The legendary is at the trip's wild level, twice its normal size and with double HP. Its ability is Hyperspace Guard, so it can't be knocked out and you have to catch it. It has the normal shiny chance, better with your shiny rolls. Only the player it belongs to can fight it, and other players can't see it. Catching it gets you the Pokémon, back in its normal form, plus the legendary mission reward. Its ability changes to a normal one when you catch it.

While your own legendary is waiting or alive, normal Pokémon don't spawn for you.

The Mega is level 200, also double size and HP, with the ability Hyperspace Mega (doubles its HP). Its shiny chance is normal. You can't catch it, but anyone can fight it, and beating it gives its Mega Stone to each player in the battle.

The legendaries come from the legendaries Pokémon tag. Only species your Cobblemon has that can walk or fly are used: Kyogre, Groudon, Deoxys, Tornadus, Thundurus, Landorus, Zygarde, Volcanion, Tapu Koko, Tapu Lele, Tapu Bulu, Tapu Fini, Zeraora, Kubfu, Zarude, Okidogi, Munkidori, Fezandipiti, Ogerpon and Terapagos. If one of them has the distortion's type, it gets picked. Kyogre and Groudon show up in their Primal form and go back to normal when caught.

The Megas can be any Mega form from Mega Showdown, and it tries to pick one with the trip's type.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
Every island has 3 tasks, shown at the top left of your screen (they're hidden during battles). Everyone on the island shares them. The tasks can be:

  • Defeat 3 Pokémon.
  • Catch 3 Pokémon.
  • Destroy 3 Hyperspace Poké Balls.
  • Quick battle and defeat 5 Pokémon.

Each finished task gives every player on the island 1 EXP Candy: XS at 1 star, S at 2, M at 3, L at 4 and XL at 5. Finish all three and each player gets a Golden Floating Poké Ball on the island (once per player) and the Taskmaster advancement.

If the island has a legendary, there's an extra mission, "Catch or defeat the legendary Pokémon.". It gives an Enchanted Golden Apple and 3 EXP Candy.

docs.title: Floating Poké Balls
docs.text:
Each island has 6 Floating Poké Balls. You can't punch them. You'll need to send out a Pokémon and hit them with one of its moves. You can learn more about how to do that here.

A normal ball drops 1 to 3 rolls of the Floating Poké Ball loot, and a golden ball drops the golden loot. Item counts go up with the trip's stars, with full amounts at 5 stars. You can learn more about the loot here.

If you have CobbleDollars installed, each ball also gives you money: 2,500 for a normal ball or 10,000 for a golden one, times the stars out of 5. So a normal ball gives 500 at 1 star, up to 2,500 at 5 stars.

Pop all 6 on an island (between any players) for the Professional Popper advancement.

docs.title: Music
docs.text: Hyperspace has its own music, and it keeps playing through battles. If you have Reactive Music installed, it gets turned down while you're in Hyperspace.

docs.title: Item Analyser Machine
docs.text: The Item Analyser is a machine that pulls a Pokémon through a small wormhole. It's built from two Cobblemon blocks. The mod renames Cobblemon's Fossil Analyzer to Item Analyser.

docs.title: Building The Machine
docs.text:
1. Place an Item Analyser (Cobblemon's Fossil Analyzer).
  2. Put a Data Monitor (Cobblemon's Monitor) directly on top of it.
  3. If you want to power it with lightning, put a Lightning Rod directly on top of the Data Monitor.
  4. Leave some open space behind the Data Monitor (the side opposite its screen). The Pokémon comes out about 5 blocks that way.

Both blocks use Cobblemon's own recipes.

Item Analyser (Fossil Analyzer):

Data Monitor:

The mod adds a way to repair a Damaged Data Monitor too. Put it in the middle of a crafting table with 8 Iron Ingots around it and you get a Data Monitor back.

docs.title: Loading The Machine
docs.text:
The machine needs a summoning recipe loaded before it does anything. Right-click the Item Analyser with the items, one of each. To take the last one back out, right-click it with an empty hand.

There are two recipes:

  • Any type gem and Blaze Powder - summons a Pokémon of the gem's type.
  • A full Jar of Cosmic Energy and a Golden Apple - summons Cosmog at level 5, and you get an Empty Jar back. A jar that isn't full won't go in.

Server owners can turn the Cosmog recipe off with the Cosmog Summon setting.

docs.title: Powering The Machine
docs.text: The Data Monitor's screen stays off until it's charged. You can charge it with lightning or with an Electric move.

docs.title: Lightning
docs.text: When lightning hits the Lightning Rod on top of the Data Monitor, the machine starts straight away if a recipe is loaded. After the summon there's a 90% chance the Data Monitor burns out into a Damaged Data Monitor.

docs.title: Electric Moves
docs.text:
1. Load a recipe into the Item Analyser.
  2. Start a quick battle with the Data Monitor by holding the Target key while looking at it.
  3. Use an Electric move on it. The screen lights up in the loaded gem's type colour (yellow if there's no gem) and plays a sound.
  4. Right-click the Data Monitor's screen to use the charge and start the machine.

The charge stays until you use it, so you don't have to start the machine straight away.

Warning

The hit can break the Data Monitor. The chance is the move's power divided by 150, up to 90%. So Thunder Shock (40 power) breaks it about 27% of the time, and Thunderbolt (90 power) 60% of the time. Moves with no listed power count as 60. Any move that isn't Electric always breaks it.

Server owners can stop Data Monitors from breaking with the Data Monitor Griefing setting. You can learn more about the settings here.

docs.title: What Comes Out
docs.text:
With a type gem and Blaze Powder there's a 95% chance of a regular Pokémon of the gem's type. It comes from the Pokémon behind the red, green, yellow and blue wormholes, all four together. If none of those has the gem's type, you get any of them. They're level 60. You can learn more about changing these Pokémon here.

The other 5% is an Ultra Beast of the gem's type at level 75. If no Ultra Beast has that type, you always get a regular Pokémon instead. Pokémon always come out at least average size.

Regular Pokémon have a 1% shiny chance, the same as a wormhole with no rings. That follows the Shiny Odds: No Rings setting, which is 1 in 100 by default. Legendaries, mythicals, Ultra Beasts and paradox Pokémon use Cobblemon's normal shiny rate, unless it's changed in the settings.

docs.title: Cooldown And Other Rules
docs.text:
• After a summon the machine overheats for 5 minutes. Clicking the screen then shows "Error" and how long is left.
  • Each summon has a 10% chance to add 1 energy to an Empty or Partially Filled Jar in your inventory.
  • Your first summon gives the Magical Summoner advancement, and summoning Cosmog gives Sun & Moon.
  • You can't break the machine's blocks while it's running.

docs.title: Ultra Space Destinations
docs.text: Ultra Space is where the wormholes of the Ultra Warp Ride take you. Each wormhole colour leads somewhere different, and most of them have a Pokémon waiting for you.

docs.title: Rules In Every Ultra Space World
docs.text:
You can't break or place blocks, use buckets, or use items on blocks (flint and steel, bone meal, hoes and so on). Doors, buttons, riding, throwing Poké Balls and right-clicking Pokémon all still work, and creative players can still build.

Each world is a set area with an invisible wall around it. The way home is the only way out, on foot or on any mount. Walk or fly into it to go back to where your ride started.

Pokémon that came out of a wormhole never move from their spot and don't despawn. They're removed once every player has left that world. If you have Waystones installed, you can't use them there.

The Ultra Space worlds reset every time the world loads, so if you log out inside one you'll be sent home when you log back in.

Ultra Beasts never spawn on their own anywhere. They only come from wormholes and the Item Analyser.

Visiting every Ultra Space world (the Ultra Warp tunnel counts too) gives the No Location Untouched advancement.

docs.title: Ultra Space Wilds (Red, Green, Yellow, Blue Wormholes)
docs.text:
The Ultra Space Wilds are four worlds, each built 1:1 from the area in Ultra Sun & Ultra Moon. You land in front of the world's exit hole, which is where the way home opens. The wormhole's Pokémon waits as a shadow at the world's hiding place until you come near.

These are the Pokémon you'll find in each one by default:

Wormhole World Regular Pokémon Legendaries Red Cliff World (floats above a sea of clouds) Swellow, Altaria, Yanmega, Sigilyph, Swanna, Drifblim, Skarmory, Togekiss Articuno, Zapdos, Moltres, Cresselia, Ho-Oh, Tornadus, Thundurus, Yveltal, Rayquaza, Landorus Green Crag World (rocky plain) Nuzleaf, Grumpig, Drapion, Audino, Heliolisk, Golurk, Ferrothorn, Bronzong, Granbull Mewtwo, Cobalion, Terrakion, Virizion, Raikou, Entei, Dialga, Reshiram, Zekrom, Xerneas Yellow Cave World Magcargo, Medicham, Hippowdon, Abomasnow, Crustle, Sableye, Steelix, Clefable Regirock, Regice, Registeel, Groudon, Palkia, Heatran, Regigigas, Giratina Blue Water World Quagsire, Lombre, Floatzel, Stunfisk, Barbaracle, Jellicent, Azumarill Uxie, Mesprit, Azelf, Lugia, Latias, Latios, Kyogre, Suicune, Kyurem

Every Wilds Pokémon is level 60. Species your Cobblemon doesn't have yet are skipped. Some Ultra Beasts without a world of their own live in the Wilds too (more on that below).

These lists come from a pool file for each colour, so a datapack can change them. You can learn more about the pool files here.

docs.title: Legendary Chance
docs.text:
The legendary chance depends on the rings and how far you'd flown when you went in. Take the light-years you'd flown, divide by 500 and round down, up to 10. That's the "light-year band" (b) in this table:

Rings Legendary chance Example at 5,000+ light-years (b = 10) 0 3% 3% 1 (b + 2)% 12% 2 (3b + 4)% 34% 3 always 100%

A legendary you don't own yet is 4 times as likely to be picked as one you already own. Some only come if you have certain legendaries in your party:

Legendary Needs in your party Rayquaza Kyogre and Groudon Landorus Tornadus and Thundurus Suicune Entei and Raikou Kyurem Reshiram and Zekrom Giratina Dialga and Palkia

Cosmog, Cosmoem, Solgaleo and Lunala never come from wormholes.

Server owners can turn wormhole legendaries off with the Wormhole Legendaries setting. The Wilds then only have regular Pokémon. You can learn more about the settings here.

docs.title: Shiny Chance (Regular Pokémon)
docs.text:
The longer you've flown, the closer a ringed wormhole gets to its full shiny odds. It reaches them at 5,000 light-years (b = 10). The default chances are:

Rings Full odds (5,000+ light-years) b = 2 b = 4 b = 6 b = 8 0 1 in 100 (1%) 1% 1% 1% 1% 1 1 in 10 (10%) 2% 4% 6% 8% 2 1 in 5 (20%) 3.1% 7.3% 11.6% 15.8% 3 1 in 3 (33%) 3.8% 11.2% 18.6% 25.9%

Under 1,000 light-years (b of 0 or 1) every wormhole has the no-ring odds. Legendaries and Ultra Beasts use Cobblemon's normal shiny rate instead, unless it's changed in the settings. Server owners can change all four odds in the settings, and the chances in between move the same way.

docs.title: Alpha Chance
docs.text: Any wormhole Pokémon can also be an alpha: 2% with no rings, 5% with 1 ring, 8% with 2 and 11% with 3.

docs.title: Ultra Beast Worlds (White Wormholes)
docs.text:
White wormholes lead to the Ultra Beast worlds. The wormhole's rings decide which Ultra Beast's world you get. The Ultra Beast stands at its spot in that world, at level 60 with the normal shiny rate.

Ultra Beast World 0 rings 1 ring 2 rings 3 rings Nihilego Ultra Deep Sea 57.7% 1.8% 0.9% 0.9% Buzzwole Ultra Jungle 17.3% 2.7% 0.9% 0.9% Pheromosa Ultra Desert 16.3% 2.7% 0.9% 0.9% Xurkitree Ultra Plant 1.9% 63.4% 17.4% 4.6% Kartana Crag World (Wilds) 1.0% 8.9% 21.7% 13.8% Celesteela Ultra Crater 1.0% 8.9% 21.7% 13.8% Guzzlord Crag World (Wilds) 1.0% 0.9% 13.0% 45.9% Necrozma Ultra Megalopolis 1.0% 0.9% 0.9% 0.9% Stakataka Crag World (Wilds) 1.0% 3.6% 8.7% 7.3% Blacephalon Cave World (Wilds) 1.0% 3.6% 8.7% 7.3% Poipole Water World (Wilds) 1.0% 2.7% 5.2% 3.7%

These assume your Cobblemon has every species. Missing ones are skipped and the rest share their chance. Ultra Beasts that live in the Wilds wait as a shadow, like the Wilds' own Pokémon.

You never catch Necrozma from a wormhole. A white wormhole to the Ultra Megalopolis starts the Necrozma boss fight instead. After 12 white wormholes in a row without it, your next white wormhole always goes there (until you've beaten Necrozma once). You can learn more about the fight here.

Each world has its own quirks:

  • Ultra Deep Sea - Nihilego's sealed cave in a world of water. Nothing drowns there and nothing hostile spawns. You walk on the sea floor with lighter gravity.
  • Ultra Jungle - Buzzwole waits down in the jungle and leaps up to its spot when you get close.
  • Ultra Desert - Pheromosa's white sand valley leading to the gem plaza.
  • Ultra Plant - Xurkitree's three towers. Statues of Xurkitree stand all over, and the real one wakes up when lightning strikes it as you come near. Lightning strikes there now and then.
  • Ultra Crater - Celesteela's crater plateau. The giant Celesteela filling the big craters are just for show. The one you can catch is giant too, and it shrinks back to normal size when caught. To battle it, send out a Pokémon while looking at its body. Cobblemon doesn't have Celesteela yet, so you'll need a mod that adds it, like Cobblemon: Myths and Legends Compat.
  • Ultra Megalopolis - the top of the Megalo Tower, alone in space. You can only walk around up there. It's where you fight Necrozma.

docs.title: Purple Wormholes
docs.text:
A purple wormhole drops you in the sky near a structure in your world, with a way home behind you. If you're riding a flying Pokémon you stay in the air. If not, you land on the ground below. No Pokémon waits at a purple wormhole.

More rings mean rarer structures. If you have Dungeons and Taverns or Legendary Monuments installed, purple wormholes can take you to their structures too:

  • No rings - villages and Cobblemon structures.
  • 1 ring - vanilla structures, and Dungeons and Taverns taverns.
  • 2 rings - large Dungeons and Taverns structures, and Legendary Monuments sites without a legendary.
  • 3 rings - Legendary Monuments shrines and the Dungeons and Taverns End Castle.

If it can't find one of that kind, it uses a lower tier.

docs.title: Waystones: Warp Stone Rides
docs.text:
If you have Waystones installed, your legend can fly you to your waystones.

  1. Give your legend a Warp Stone to hold.
  2. Open a wormhole and fly into it like normal.
  3. The tunnel has one wormhole for each of your activated waystones, coloured by the waystone's dimension. Fly into the one you want.

After those comes one green "uncharted" wormhole that leads somewhere far off in your world.

docs.title: Ultra Warp Ride
docs.text: The Ultra Warp Ride is the one from Ultra Sun & Ultra Moon. You fly down a tunnel through Ultra Space and pick a wormhole to fly into.

docs.title: What You Need
docs.text:
You need a Solgaleo, Lunala, Dusk Mane Necrozma or Dawn Wings Necrozma that you own. The mod makes Solgaleo and Lunala rideable and lets them fly. Plain Necrozma and Ultra Necrozma can't open wormholes.

You also have to be riding it and flying. That means in the air, with some air below you, and not touching the ground or water.

Server owners can change which mounts are allowed in config/hyperspace_wormholes.json. You can learn more about that here.

docs.title: Opening A Wormhole
docs.text:
1. Get on your legend and fly up into the air.
  2. Press V (the "Open Wormhole" key under "Cobblemon: Hyperspace & Wormholes" in Controls). Your legend roars and a wormhole opens about 14 blocks ahead of you.
  3. Fly straight into it. It only lasts 10 seconds and takes one rider.

Players riding on your legend with you come along too. Your first ride gives the Ride Of Your Life advancement.

You can roar again after 7.5 seconds. Once you've started a ride though, you have to wait 2.5 minutes (counted from the start of that ride) before the next one. Until then you'll see "You can travel through a wormhole again in ...". Roaring doesn't work in Hyperspace ("... tried to open a wormhole, but failed.").

docs.title: Flying The Tunnel
docs.text:
Once you're in, you steer around the tunnel with W, A, S and D. "Ultra Space Travelled" shows how far you've flown in light-years.

The stamina bar has 18 sections and one drains every 5 seconds. When it runs out, your legend gets dragged into the next wormhole. Fly through the golden rings to refill a section and get a short speed boost. Each ring also makes you 3% faster for the rest of the ride, but stamina drains 3% faster too.

Wormholes come up about every 210 light-years. Fly into the one you want. The screen goes white and you come out where it leads.

docs.title: Wormhole Colours
docs.text:
By default the wormholes use the game's colours:

Colour Leads to First appears Red Ultra Space Wilds: Cliff World from the start Green Ultra Space Wilds: Crag World (Rocky World) from the start Yellow Ultra Space Wilds: Cave World from the start Blue Ultra Space Wilds: Water World from the start Purple The sky above a structure in your world after 2,000 light-years White An Ultra Beast world after 4,500 light-years

Red, green, yellow and blue are a quarter each of the regular wormholes. Once purple can appear, it's about 10% of the non-white wormholes. White gets more likely the further you fly: 12.5% up to 10,000 light-years, 25% up to 20,000, 37.5% up to 30,000 and 50% after that.

You can learn more about what's past each colour here. If you have Waystones installed, giving your legend a Warp Stone changes the tunnel so it can fly you to your waystones. You can learn more about that here.

docs.title: Rings
docs.text:
Wormholes can have 0 to 3 golden rings around them. More rings mean better odds past them. Rings only start showing up after 1,000 light-years:

Light-years flown 0 rings 1 ring 2 rings 3 rings under 1,000 100% - - - 1,000-1,499 78% 20% 2% - 1,500-1,999 66% 30% 4% - 2,000-2,499 52% 40% 8% - 2,500-2,999 33% 50% 16% 1% 3,000-3,499 32% 50% 16% 2% 3,500-3,999 31% 50% 16% 3% 4,000-4,499 30% 50% 16% 4% 4,500 and up 29% 50% 16% 5%

Server owners can change how often each ring count shows up in the settings file (wormholeRingWeights). Going into a 3-ring wormhole gives the Maximum Rings advancement.

docs.title: Cosmic Jar
docs.text:
The Cosmic Jar is how you get Cosmog. You fill it with cosmic energy as you travel, then use it in the Item Analyser.

Craft an Empty Jar on a crafting table (shaped):

If you have a jar that isn't full anywhere in your inventory, there's a 10% chance to add 1 cosmic energy to it. This happens each time you start a ride, come out of a wormhole, come home or summon something with the Item Analyser. The jar holds 4. It starts as an Empty Jar, then it's a Partially Filled Jar, and once it's full it's a Jar of Cosmic Energy (it shines).

Once it's full, put it in the Item Analyser with a Golden Apple to summon Cosmog.

docs.title: Getting Unstuck
docs.text: If you get stuck on a ride, /wormhole unstuck ends it and takes you back on foot to where it started. Your mount goes back in its ball. It only works during a ride.
